name: Vespid Dynamics Intercept Swarm IVS-7 'Hornet Veil'
product_name: Vespid Dynamics Intercept Swarm IVS-7 'Hornet Veil'
description:
The IVS-7 is a personal active protection system consisting of 2,400 semi-autonomous nano-interceptors — each approximately 4mm in diameter — maintained in a distributed formation around the wearer at distances between 30cm and 2 meters. Each interceptor carries a micro-piezoelectric sensor array capable of detecting incoming projectiles by acoustic pressure wave and ballistic doppler signature within 8 milliseconds of muzzle discharge. The swarm's distributed processing network resolves the trajectory, assigns the three nearest interceptors to intercept, and executes a kinetic collision course — all before the projectile travels more than 4 meters.

The physics is violent and intimate. Each interceptor detonates a 0.3-gram shaped tungsten charge on contact with an incoming round, fragmenting the projectile and altering its trajectory enough to defeat ballistic penetration at the wearer's position. Against standard 9x19mm and 5.56mm rounds, the IVS-7 achieves 91% deflection rate in controlled testing. Against caseless high-velocity rounds, the rate drops to 74%. Against coilgun penetrators with magnetically hardened cores — which the interceptors' own electromagnetic fields partially guide toward them — the rate climbs back to 88%. Plasma and laser weapons the swarm cannot engage at all.

In GLMZ, the Hornet Veil has reshaped how Tier 4 and 5 security operates. The soft hum of an active swarm is now a recognizable sound in high-tier corporate lobbies and armored motorcades — a sound that means someone in the room has decided they are worth protecting at this level. On the Gray Zone, the sound means something else: whoever is wearing the swarm is not someone you can simply shoot. The interceptors are visible to the naked eye as a faint shimmering distortion, like heat haze with purpose. People who have seen one activate describe the experience as watching the air bite a bullet.

tactical_use: The IVS-7 is a bodyguard multiplier, not a replacement for cover. Against uncoordinated fire from 1-3 shooters, the swarm functions as advertised — an executive or VIP can move through a kill zone that would stop conventional armor cold. Against coordinated suppressive fire from 5+ automatic weapons, the swarm becomes saturated: it can only process and intercept projectiles faster than it can recharge interceptors. Volume fire defeats it within 40-60 seconds. Smart counters: EMP grenades, laser/plasma weapons, and the specific 12.7mm EMP-core round (which the swarm's own electromagnetic targeting will preferentially attract before the EMP discharge). Trained operators aim slightly wide of the target and let the swarm do what it's designed for — spend resources defeating rounds that don't need defeating.
cultural_context: The IVS-7 costs Φ340,000 for a base system and Φ18,000 per full interceptor resupply. This means only Tier 4+ individuals — corporate executives, senior security contractors, A and S-tier freelancers with very profitable recent work — can operate one. It has become a status symbol so potent that wearing an inactive swarm carrier (with no interceptors loaded) has become a fashion statement in certain Tier 3 circles. Knockoffs exist: dead swarms, decommissioned units with depleted interceptors, even entirely non-functional prop carriers. The phrase 'flying empty swarm' has entered GLMZ slang meaning someone projecting more protection or power than they actually have.
known_users: A and S-tier freelancers on major contracts
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone-district repair shop is offering IVS-7 interceptor resupply at Φ800 per batch — one-fifth the going rate. The interceptors work. Nobody can explain where they're coming from.
A client hires Kyle to escort them through a location where the IVS-7 swarm's EMP signature will be detected — they need protection but can't announce they're worth protecting.
